newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares jump after US surge, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares jump after US surge, dollar steady.

text.p: Key European stock markets advanced in early trading on Wednesday in the wake of Wall Street's second-largest daily points gain overnight but at a slightly slower pace than in New York.
The Paris bourse and the London stock market, Europe's busiest, were up 1.2 and 0.9 percent by mid-morning, compared with a 2.60 percent gain on the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue chips.
In Frankfurt, shares were around two percent ahead, while key indices in Amsterdam rose 1.8 percent, Zurich one percent and Milan 1.3 percent.
On currency markets, the dollar held steady, below overnight highs but above 1.71 marks and 126 yen.

Investors in New York charged into the perceived safety of top-name blue-chip shares, while U.S. bonds strengthened after a successful Treasury note auction. But analysts said they were less sure about prospects for the broader U.S. share market.
The Dow Jones industrial average of 30 blue chips ended up 173.38 points, or 2.60 percent, at 6,833.59.
In points terms, this was the second largest gain after an 187-point leap two days after the "Black Monday" stock market crash of October 1987, when the Dow lost 508 points.

Despite recent speculation that European bourses might decouple from market developments in the world's biggest economy, the New York gains were the key factor in morning business on this side of the Atlantic.
London shares raced ahead from the start in trading given extra spice by an opinion poll suggesting a much reduced lead for the opposition Labour Party ahead of next week's May 1 election.
"We had a predictable mark-up on the back of Wall Street but there is still a lot of uncertainty out there," said a senior dealer.
"The latest opinion poll, if true, suggests there could be a hung parliament. That is something the market does not want to see," he said.

The ICM poll in The Guardian newspaper slashed Labour's lead from 14 to five points, the first time it has slipped to single figures since November 1993. But Gallup's survey in the Daily Telegraph put the gap up five points to 21.

"We'll stay around these levels until we get more of a clue what Wall Street's going to do this afternoon. There's not much business behind this rise although there are still a lot of short positions," said another London dealer.
German shares made rapid progress, spurred on by New York's example, but could not match the jump in U.S. stocks as earnings news from industrial giant Siemens disappointed investors.
Shares in Siemens fell 90 pfennigs to 90 marks in pre-bourse trade immediately after news of flat profits although they later recovered to 90.40.
French shares rallied just over one percent at the opening, reviving from a depression caused by political uncertainty ahead of this week's news of French parliamentary elections from late May.
Traders said Wall Street's rise and firmer bonds helped, as well as a more relaxed reading of the French political situation.

"The political risk is not so tremendous," one Paris broker said. The French government is seeking to confirm its position in power ahead of taking tough measures to ensure qualification for European economic and monetary union.
Currency trading was less energetic, although dealers said the Dow's gains and firmer U.S. bonds gave some light support to the dollar.

"The stronger U.S. assets appear to be more technically driven and that alone is not likely to give the dollar much motivation higher from current levels," cautioned Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.
In New York trading the dollar had strengthened after German economists predicted it would rally in the coming months and U.S. negotiators reportedly neared a deal on the federal budget.

Dealers said trade was likely to remain quiet ahead of a meeting of finance ministers of the Group of Seven major industrial nations in Washington this weekend and Friday's meeting between Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Another market focus would be the European Commission's spring economic forecasts, announced after a delay on Wednesday morning.

These showed leading EU countries except Italy would reach the budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product for monetary union. Italy's deficit was put at 3.2 percent of GDP this year.
In trading between European currencies, the French franc, after uncertainties on the political scene, was steady around 3.3735 to the mark versus 3.3758 overnight.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7145 marks and 126.18 yen after ending at 1.7131 and 126.21 in late trading in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 38.6 points or 0.89 percent at 4,384.7.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 59.25 points or 1.77 percent higher at 3,399.58.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 29.22 points or 1.16 percent at 2,543.89.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.70 an ounce, compared with Tuesday's London close of $341.65. Silver slipped three cents to $4.73.
